newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine gov't unsure of pension cost - papers.
newsitem.headline: Argentine gov't unsure of pension cost - papers.

text.p: The Argentine government is still calculating the cost of Friday's court ruling retroactively granting 70,000 pensioners an extra payment to cover the 1991 to 1994 period, President Carlos Menem said in comments reported Monday.
"The calculations have to be done and instruments established that put us up to date on the issue," Menem told newspapers in his home province of La Rioja.

The Argentine media speculated that the Supreme Court ruling could cost the government no more than $700 million, shared out over the 1997 and 1998 fiscal years, with most of the payments made in 1998.
The court ruled that the government must pay the pensioners a 13.8 percent rise for the period from 1991 to 1994. It is unclear as to when and how the money will be paid.
